Phase 62 impl @ a9ea621 (branch phase/framework-provenance-from-earlier-releases). gate: see entry @ a9ea621 — I did not run the full suite.

What changed
- tagteam/data/history/<last-tag>/…: the 13 earlier sources, written straight from git show <tag>:tagteam/data/<source_rel>; pyproject.toml glob data/history/**/*.md.
- tagteam/framework.py: _history_sources() (newest first by parsed version, [] on any read problem), _tag_key(), one evidence step in _classify() after the manifest / known-contract / current-package-render checks and before custom: verbatim, then the existing _render_variants() over the historical bytes -> FRAMEWORK + reconstructible, reason 'written by tagteam ≤X (rendered for the configured|swapped names)'. build_plan() passes history for managed and retired items, not the skill. _prune_retired_dirs(): ENOTEMPTY/EEXIST silent, anything else -> Plan.unpruned_dirs -> 'kept <dir>/ — directory left in place (<why>)', not a refusal. No change to apply(), projected_manifest(), preimage rechecks, setup.py, bench.py.
- Docs: tagteam/data/workflows.md, README.md, CLAUDE.md (history/ is frozen), roadmap backlog entry closed. This repo's docs/workflows.md refreshed by the new setup (manifest hash), manifest now 3.14.0.

Your plan-approval notes
- _old_project's synthetic phase_plan.md fixture is untouched and still asserted custom/kept. Added an exact v3.11.0 feedback.md rendered claude/codex (matching its config) for the installed-wheel retire assertion; that is also the wheel-contains-history proof.
- Table test (test_history_table_is_what_git_history_says) checks both tagteam/data and ai_handoff/data prefixes, asserts byte equality per file AND that history ∪ current covers every distinct sha shipped at tags <= v3.12.0 with nothing invented; skips only when v3.12.0 is not among local tags. It ran (not skipped) here.
- Manifest-first order unchanged and pinned: test_manifest_match_is_still_decided_first. Docs say 'exact copies … through 3.12.0', and that renamed agents or any edit means the file is the owner's — no claim that every earlier copy is retired.
- Exact-byte matching only; names come from tagteam.yaml via the existing get_template_variables, nothing inferred from file text.

Criterion 10 — real registry, tagteam upgrade --preview, 41 projects, nothing written (3.14.0 -> this branch): retire 184 -> 480, keep 332 -> 0, refresh workflows.md 4 -> 41, refuse 0 -> 0. Reasons: 296 '≤3.11.0 (rendered for the configured names)', 184 'matches the package'; workflows 35 '≤3.10.0', 1 '≤3.11.0', 5 manifest hash. Table is in the phase doc.

Verified by me: focused only — tests/test_framework.py 75 passed (14 new under the 'Phase 62' banner), tests/test_upgrade_smoke.py 12 passed. Not done: release 3.14.1 and the real sweep (after merge).

Bounce: 1 failed / 2057 passed — tests/test_plugin.py::TestShippedDocsAudit::test_no_legacy_command_family. A real conflict, not a flake: history/v3.10.0/workflows.md (the pre-plugin doc) has 45 /handoff-* lines and Phase 49 forbids shipping any. The other 12 sources are clean.

Fix, and a DEVIATION from approved Scope 4 ('sources, not a sha table') — please rule on it: I did not exempt data/history/ from the audit. That one file now ships as history/v3.10.0/workflows.md.sha256. _history_sources() returns (tag, sha, bytes|None); _classify() marks a digest-only match FRAMEWORK with reconstructible=False and skips rendering for it. Effect: docs/workflows.md refresh needs provenance only (same as manifest / known-contract refresh), so the 35 real copies still refresh; a digest-only match on a retired path would fall to Phase 61's git rule by construction (none exists). Cost stated in the phase doc: the overwritten v3.10.0 text is not reproducible from the installed package. Alternative if you prefer it: keep the text and exempt history/ in the audit — one line, but it makes 'nothing tagteam ships mentions /handoff-*' false.

Changed since round 1: tagteam/framework.py (_history_sources, _classify, docstring), pyproject.toml glob data/history/**/*.sha256, tests/test_framework.py (table test verifies the digest against git show v3.10.0; ordering test asserts digest-only for v3.10.0; v3.10.0 refresh test takes its bytes from git and skips without tags, and asserts reconstructible == (tag != v3.10.0)), CLAUDE.md, phase doc 'Deviation' section.

Verified by me: tests/test_framework.py + tests/test_plugin.py 140 passed (includes the audit); tests/test_upgrade_smoke.py 12 passed; pip wheel of the tree contains 13 data/history entries incl. the .sha256 (built in scratch, build/ + egg-info cleared). Approved implementation at 386261b, including the explicitly submitted deviation to digest-only provenance for v3.10.0/workflows.md. This is consistent with existing managed-file refresh semantics: an exact known hash proves framework provenance, while reconstructible=False correctly prevents a digest-only retired file from bypassing Phase 61 recovery rules. The documented limitation is accepted: the old workflow bytes cannot be recovered from the installed package itself. The unchanged shipped-docs audit now passes without distributing obsolete command instructions.

Reviewed the production diff, history inventory/tag-pinning tests, name-rendering and custom-file preservation coverage, prune-error reporting, installed-wheel fixture, and registry preview results. The synthetic custom phase_plan.md remains protected; the separate exact historical feedback.md exercises retirement from the installed wheel. Manifest-first classification and deletion preimage checks are preserved. No blocking findings.
